statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail rests at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains well below the block threshold. One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where untested September rate pricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: the weekend halt holds tail risk at the low-band floor while a chip-led Friday pullback sits beside near-coin-flip September rate pricing
body:
This assessment falls inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The anchor is Friday's completed session, re-verified against the ^NDX quote page this hour and unchanged: NDX opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.56 previous close, leaving the close roughly 50 points off the low of a 369-point range. That is a downside reversal in a finished session, and the Nasdaq still ended the week higher, so it reads as rotation rather than an extending trend. VIX closed 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range, carrying no volatility premium into the weekend.

This hour adds one causal detail to the internal composition. Friday's weakness was concentrated in semiconductors, and the named driver is Nvidia's notification to clients of price increases above 15% on Vera Rubin and Blackwell servers shipping in early 2027. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context shows all seven tracked chip names lower, led by ARM and Nvidia, while Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet closed higher. A sector margin repricing that leaves other megacaps bid is not the index-wide one-way structure this Tail measure tracks.

The open question remains policy pricing rather than price structure. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote was read as hawkish, with PCE cited at 3.7% over twelve months, and September rate-hike pricing moved from roughly 35% to about 57-59% on CME-based futures while prediction markets sat closer to 48%. H.15 constant-maturity yields for 27 August still read 2Y 4.20%, 5Y 4.38%, 10Y 4.67% and 30Y 5.19%, with no weekend update, so the official series does not yet capture the post-keynote move. That repricing has not met a live tape since Friday's close, which is why it sits in Stress rather than Tail.

Geopolitical transmission remains contained. Strait of Hormuz traffic is still well below normal with shipping risk assessed as severe, but WTI near 83.44 is roughly unchanged as Gulf export flows partially recover, so the disruption is currently absorbed rather than repricing energy. The week ahead is dense: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Beige Book on Wednesday with Broadcom results after the close, ISM Services on Thursday, and August payrolls on Friday against a prior print of -23K. Those are scheduled checkpoints, not observed conditions, so they support Stress at 26 and Confidence at 79 while Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5. The single flagged observation window covers the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where untested September rate pricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, spanning the weekend halt from Saturday afternoon through this morning. The series was uniformly green with Tail held at 5, dominant mode normal and Stress confined to a 25-26 band. Confidence decayed from 72 to 58 as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered through 64, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77 and 78 as primary sources were re-verified on successive refreshes. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next nine projected hours remain inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 26 to 29 as the reopen approaches and Confidence decays from 79 to 71 with ageing evidence. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen tonight the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and far below the block threshold, covering the first live test of near-coin-flip September rate pricing, thin reopen liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases through 11, 10 and 9 across the Asian session to 8 into the European morning on an assumed orderly repricing, before returning to 9 at the European open and again into Monday's pre-US-open build-up. Every projected hour maps to EA_ON. All values beyond the current clock hour are conditional; no reopen or overnight structure has been observed, and repeated extension after failed retracements would be the evidence that invalidates this path.
